text:
amar: heads-up — I kicked off 3 parallel terraform import jobs against staging to move some resources between modules. now terraform apply is failing with a lock error and the plan is showing a bunch of subnet_group resources as tainted/recreate. anyone seen this after parallel imports?

jamie: which workspace? any chance a CI apply is still running? paste the exact error if you can.

amar: workspace=staging. error snippet: ```
Error: Error locking state: Error acquiring the state lock: ConditionalCheckFailedException: The conditional request failed
  on backend.tf line 12, in resource "aws_dynamodb_table" "tf_locks":
 12: resource "aws_dynamodb_table" "tf_locks" {}
```
Plus plan shows ~8 aws_db_subnet_group resources will be replaced.

rachel: ok first checks: 1) confirm no active CI job holding the lock 2) check dynamodb lock table for the lock id (we use tfstate-locks table in staging).
Commands: ```
# list locks (approx)
aws dynamodb scan --table-name tfstate-locks --region us-west-2 --limit 20
# or if you have lock id
aws dynamodb get-item --table-name tfstate-locks --key '{"LockID":{"S":"<LOCK_ID>"}}' --region us-west-2
```
If it's stale and no apply running, `terraform force-unlock <LOCK_ID>` is fine. Don't force-unlock if CI is mid-apply.

nate: adding caution — we had a case where folks reimport -> force-unlock -> reimport again and state had duplicate addresses causing plan to replace things. check `terraform state list | grep aws_db_subnet_group` and look for duplicates or wrong module addresses.

amar: ran `terraform state list | grep subnet_group` and got:```
module.network.aws_db_subnet_group.example
aws_db_subnet_group.example
```
Looks like some were imported into the root module and others into `module.network` (that's my mistake).

jamie: that's the root cause. When the resource address differs from where the config expects it, plan will think it needs to recreate. Two options: 1) move state to the correct address with `terraform state mv` 2) re-import using the correct address so state references match config. For many resources, `state mv` is quickest. Example: `terraform state mv aws_db_subnet_group.example module.network.aws_db_subnet_group.example`

rachel: +1 to state mv if you verified the imported resource is actually the same physical resource. If you move state, run a `terraform plan -target=module.network.aws_db_subnet_group.example` first to confirm no diffs.

amar: ok I did `terraform state mv aws_db_subnet_group.example module.network.aws_db_subnet_group.example` for the ones that were in root. Then `terraform plan -target=module.network.aws_db_subnet_group.example` shows no change.

infra-bot: detected lock activity: lock id `lk-0a1b2c3d` removed by amar at 2023-11-02T15:01:40Z

nate: nice. one more gotcha — provider alias mismatch can also cause recreate. if you see `provider["registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/aws"].alias != expected` in `terraform state show` then the resource's provider meta needs fixing.

amar: discovered a provider alias mismatch for one resource (imported with the default provider but config uses `provider.aws.uswest2`), re-imported that one with the right provider config and everything looks clean now.

jamie: great. TL;DR for others: avoid running parallel imports against the same state; if you do and you end up with mixed addresses: check `terraform state list`, reconcile with `state mv` or re-import with correct address, verify with `plan -target`, then force-unlock only after confirming no active apply. :thumbsup:

amar: thanks all — resolved. will not parallel-import the same workspace again. :relieved:
